criteria: States both papers' length, marks and weightings correctly, and divides 80 marks into 40 reading and 40 writing
Recalls Paper 1 Section A question marks and AOs (4 AO1, 8 AO2, 8 AO2, 20 AO4) accurately

Identifies Spoken Language as separately reported, unmarked, Pass/Merit/Distinction/Not Classified
S01_Course_Map_Papers_and_Marks.pass_threshold: Recalls each paper's length, marks, sections and question marks without prompting, explains the 4-level ladder and can say what level and mark an unseen short answer deserves and why.

Recalls the exclusion of transient text and the requirement for substantial, unseen texts
Expresses reasoning in clear, accurate sentences
S02_Texts_Periods_and_What_Sources_Look_.pass_threshold: Correctly classifies at least six unfamiliar short extracts by text type and period with reasons, and states the rule about transient content.

S03_Terminology_Word_Classes_Phrases_Cla.pass_threshold: Accurately labels the word class of ten words in context, identifies a main and subordinate clause in five sentences, and explains an effect of tense or modality in a given sentence.

Links form to effect coherently, using relevant terminology

source.document: AQA GCSE English Language 8700 specification v1.6, AO2 and AO6 in section 4.5

S05_Terminology_Figurative_and_Sound_Lan.pass_threshold: Identifies and explains at least eight devices in a supplied passage, at least five with accurate, specific effects.

criteria: Separates explicit from implicit information accurately

Uses short, judicious, embedded evidence rather than copying

Shades exactly the supported statements in Part 2 (B, C, E, F, H) and no more than four are shaded, or if more are chosen the learner recognises the maximum rule -- Paper 2 Q1's unchanged format

Works quickly and accurately (about five minutes per question)
S07_Short_Reading_Questions_P1Q1_and_P2Q.pass_threshold: Scores at least 3 of 4 on an unseen Paper 1 Q1 shade-the-boxes question and at least 3 of 4 on an unseen Paper 2 Q1 shade-the-boxes question, identifying the trap in any wrong answer.

criteria: Distinguishes fact, opinion and evidence-supported claims correctly
Identifies bias and misuse of evidence with specific reference to the text
Evaluates usefulness relative to a stated purpose
Expresses evaluation in clear, reasoned sentences

Reaches Level 3 or above by the board's descriptors
S09_Summary_and_Synthesis_P2Q2.pass_threshold: Writes an 8-mark synthesis on an unseen pair of short sources at Level 3 (5-6 marks) or above: both sources covered, differences stated with inference and selected quotations.

Zooms in on individual words and connotations

Explains effects on the reader clearly (Level 3) or perceptively (Level 4)

Links language to the writer's purpose and viewpoint
S11_Language_Analysis_Paper_2_Q3_and_Per.pass_threshold: Writes an unseen 12-mark language answer at Level 3 (7-9) or above with at least four well-explained points on a range of features, plus correctly identifies six rhetorical devices in a supplied text.

criteria: Covers beginning, middle and end of the whole extract
Identifies specific structural features (shift of focus, flashback, pace change, delayed reveal, final sentence)
From 2026, ties each structural feature back to the single effect the question names (e.g. suspense, tension, a growing sense of loss), not to 'interest' in general
Explains the effect of each choice on the reader, not only what happens
Uses accurate structural terminology
Reaches Level 3 or above on the board's descriptors
S12_Structure_Analysis_Paper_1_Q3.pass_threshold: Writes an unseen 8-mark structure response at Level 3 (5-6) or above: at least three structural features across beginning, middle and end, each with a clear effect on the reader.

source.document: AQA GCSE English Language 8700 specification v1.6, 3.1.1 (analysing and evaluating form and structure) and Paper 1 mark scheme (June 2021) Question 3 -- from 2026, AQA's Question 3 names a single structural effect to track (e.g. suspense) rather than asking generally how structure is interesting; the mark scheme's levels and marks (8, Level 1-4) are unchanged, per several independent GCSE revision publishers (Save My Exams, Think Smart Academy, Uplevel Academy) who agree on this change, confirmed directly by AQA's own published change page (aqa.org.uk/english-language-changes), which gives 'how has the writer structured the text to create suspense' as the new example wording.

criteria: Identifies perspective and tense accurately and explains their effect

Tracks focus and shifts across the extract
Links technique to the reader's response (unease, sympathy, curiosity)
S13_Reading_Fiction_Openings_Voice_and_P.pass_threshold: Correctly identifies narrative perspective, tone and the focus of an unseen fiction extract, and explains in two paragraphs how the writer uses these to engage the reader.
